lectures.title: Best Practices for Cron Jobs: Smart Scheduling, Security and Maintenance

cues.en: In this lecture, I want to talk about a few best practices when it comes to Cronjob.
So first is planning and scheduling.
So the first tip would be that we distribute the tasks evenly, but that we also try to avoid peak hours.
So for example, if we do have a computations, it's probably not the best time to do it.
While there's a lot of traffic on our site, but maybe we can just do it at night at 3 a.m. but be aware
of different time zones.
So it really depends from where you get your visitors on your website.
For example, if you're running a web server, then you might want to avoid executing the same task
multiple times at the same time, especially if the intervals that this task should run are really small,
then really consider using a tool like airflow to avoid that.
So that would be my tip for planning and scheduling.
When it comes to logging and error handling, then my tip would be that you should log errors and analyze
them regularly because something something might break.
Or maybe you push an update to your application code that will break the cron job.
But you didn't realize that.
Or it happened to me actually one time.
And then suddenly the cron job is no longer being executed or I mean it, it's being executed.
It just fails.
So my tip to myself would be to make sure that I log all errors and also that I do analyze them regularly.
We might also implement error checks within our scripts.
But then of course, it's also important that we log those errors or that we handle those errors within
our script to notify us in any way.
So that's also a really important thing.
The next thing is about security or the next things we need to pay attention to.
And there I would or the recommendation is that we run tasks with the least privilege as possible.
So even if there was a bug and they might do something else in our system, the damage can at least
be somewhat mitigated there and they can't access the whole system.
So this could already improve our security.

able to read those files, but maybe it can't change them anymore.

with the cron job might not be deleted.
So be aware of the privileges and also that if you do create files from your cron job, the privileges
or the owner of the file might be off or you might have you might have to add the commands to change

work with those files and maybe edit them or delete them.

a third party storage service.
So this would be one thing for security.

Of course, this doesn't necessarily just apply to cron jobs, but just to our application in general.
The next thing is that we should avoid storing sensitive information in crontab files, so we shouldn't
use any passwords in the crontab file.
We should not store them there.
If we do have to store them, it would be better to have separate files for that.
And then, of course, also for those files, the permissions should be as restrictive as possible.
The next thing is testing.
We should test our cronjobs before adding them to crontab.
We should be aware that cron might have a different path variable and our scripts should still work
with a different path variable.
If we want to avoid any issues, we can also just use absolute paths or set the path at the beginning

properly executed.
